nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Commercial Ni foam was cut into 2.5×2.5 cm² plates, then compressed into thinner ones to improve the wettability. Ni foam was sequentially ultrasonically treated in 3M hydrochloric acid (HCl) aqueous solution, deionized water, and ethanol to remove the surface oxides and organic molecules, then dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C.
nodes.source_text: Before the synthetic procedures, commercial Ni foam was cut into 2.5×2.5 cm² plates, then compressed into thinner ones to improve the wettability. Ni foam was sequentially ultrasonically treated in 3M hydrochloric acid (HCl) aqueous solution, deionized water, and ethanol to remove the surface oxides and organic molecules, then dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C.

nodes.name: First hydrothermal - nanowire precursor
nodes.procedure: The clean Ni foam plate was immersed in 35 mL of a uniform transparent aqueous solution containing (NH4)2HPO4 (1 mM). Then, the sealed 50 mL autoclave was retained at 180°C for different times to prepare the precursors. The achieved green precursors were washed several times with deionized water and dried in air.
nodes.source_text: First, the clean Ni foam plate was immersed in 35 mL of a uniform transparent aqueous solution containing (NH4)2HPO4 (1 mM). Then, the sealed 50 mL autoclave was retained at 180°C for different times to prepare the precursors.

nodes.name: Second hydrothermal - Ni(OH)2/NF
nodes.procedure: The green precursor was transformed into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave containing 30 mL of 0.1 M KOH aqueous solution. Subsequently, the autoclave was kept at 120°C for 5 h. After cooling to room temperature, the light gray Ni(OH)2/NF nanoarrays were rinsed with deionized water and dried in air.
nodes.source_text: In a typical procedure, the green precursor was transformed into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave containing 30 mL of 0.1 M KOH aqueous solution... dried in air.

nodes.name: Phosphorization - Ni2P/NF
nodes.procedure: The freshly obtained Ni(OH)2/NF and NaH2PO2·H2O, with a weight ratio of 1:10, were put into the same ceramic boat at two separated places, while NaH2PO2·H2O is at the upstream side. After excluding air for 30 min in flowing Ar at room temperature, the samples were maintained at 300°C for 30 min with a heating rate of 5°C/min under a flowing Ar atmosphere. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the achieved black samples were collected.

unit_operations.name: Phosphorization annealing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the samples were maintained at 300°C for 30 min with a heating rate of 5°C/min under a flowing Ar atmosphere

nodes.source_text: The Ni2P/NF was prepared via a low-temperature calcination method. The freshly obtained Ni(OH)2/NF and NaH2PO2·H2O... the achieved black samples were collected.

nodes.name: Ni-Fe LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: Clean Ni foam was put into 30 mL of a transparent light green aqueous solution containing 0.5 mM Fe(NO3)2·9H2O, 0.5 mM Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 3 mM urea, and 7.5 mM NH4F. Then the 50 mL autoclave was transferred into an oven and kept at 120°C for 6 h. After cooling to room temperature, the obtained Ni-Fe LDH was rinsed with deionized water and dried in air.
nodes.source_text: The Ni-Fe LDH was synthesized with a modified reported method. In a typical process, clean Ni foam was put into 30 mL... dried in air for further use.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: Electrocatalytic HER activities... evaluated via a three-electrode system in 1 M KOH electrolyte (pH 13.95)... Ni₂P/NF can sustain current densities of 1000 and 1500 mA cm⁻² at overpotentials of 306 and 368 mV... Tafel plots give slopes of 76 mV dec⁻¹... C_dl of Ni₂P/NF (55.2 mF cm⁻²)... R_ct of Ni₂P/NF is 3.5 Ω

nodes.description: HER stability testing in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: the long-term chronoamperometry (j-t) test shows that a high current density of 2500 mA cm⁻² can be maintained without decrease after 10 h of continuous electrolysis

nodes.description: Overall water splitting Ni₂P||Ni-Fe LDH in 1 M KOH two-electrode system
nodes.source_text: overall water splitting in a two-electrode system using 1 M KOH electrolyte. The Ni₂P/NF was used directly as the cathode... Ni-Fe LDH... as anode... Ni₂P||Ni-Fe LDH... surpasses Pt/C||Ir/C at higher current densities (>600 mA cm⁻²)... Faradaic efficiency of ∼100%
Multistep chronoamperometric curves were measured under a wide potential range (from 240 to 650 mV) ... results showed that the electrocatalytic activities remain stable at each step during the test

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show uniform nanoarray morphology of Ni₂P/NF inherited from the original Ni(OH)₂ precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM and TEM images of the obtained Ni₂P show a uniform nanoarray morphology, inherited from the original Ni(OH)₂ precursor (Figures 1b-d and S9).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructured material with fibrous or rod-like morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm uniform nanoarray morphology of Ni₂P/NF; corresponding SAED pattern reveals polycrystalline feature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding SAED pattern reveals a polycrystalline feature, which can be easily distinguished from the single-crystal-like pattern of the Ni(OH)₂ precursor (inset in Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images demonstrate distinct lattice fringes with spacing of 0.13 nm attributed to the (311) plane of hexagonal Ni₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images demonstrate distinct lattice fringes with a spacing of 0.13 nm that could be attributed to the (311) plane of hexagonal Ni₂P (JCPDS 030953), which is consistent with the results from the XRD patterns (Figures 1e,f, S10, and S11).

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing lattice fringes

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm hexagonal Ni₂P phase (JCPDS 030953) for Ni₂P/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images demonstrate distinct lattice fringes with a spacing of 0.13 nm that could be attributed to the (311) plane of hexagonal Ni₂P (JCPDS 030953), which is consistent with the results from the XRD patterns (Figures 1e,f, S10, and S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni and P in Ni₂P/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX and XPS survey spectra verify the existence of Ni and P, which are uniformly distributed, as shown in our STEM elemental mapping (Figures S12, S13a, and 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 857.2 eV (2p₃/₂) and 875.1 eV (2p₁/₂), P 2p at 134.3 eV confirming Ni₂P formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni 2p spectra analysis shows that the two obvious peaks at 857.2 and 875.1 eV can be attributed to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂. The peak at 134.3 eV originates from P 2p. These results verify the generation of Ni₂P (Figure S13b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance R_ct = 3.5 Ω for Ni₂P/NF vs 25.2 Ω for Ni(OH)₂/NF at 100 mV overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) Nyquist plots reveal that the charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of Ni₂P/NF is 3.5 Ω which is much lower than that of Ni(OH)₂/NF (25.2 Ω) and blank NF (69.5 Ω) at an overpotential of 100 mV.
